blockers.title: builderAttestation has neither a representable trust-root role nor a signature-verification algorithm
evidence: builderAttestation.verifyAgainst selects the unique certificate-store member whose originSearchPolicy or companion role token is kernel-builder-root. The exhaustive signedEntry shape has exactly {platformProfileKey, class, identityEvidence, originSearchPolicy}; the enumerated originSearchPolicy keys contain no role field or role-token grammar; and the only defined companion is SONAME-ABI, which explicitly is not a signed-entry field and never changes authenticity. No conforming location can carry the selector token.

The certificate store class allows only DIGEST-BOUND identity. DIGEST-BOUND requires a named collision-resistant digest and collection membership over bytes; it does not define a public-key format, key-use authorization, detached-signature algorithm, or signature verification operation.

builderAttestation.signature says its algorithm is what the root member's DIGEST-BOUND scheme permits, parenthetically 'codesign cdhash or package-db digest of the builder cert'. A cdhash and a package/member digest are identity values, not signature algorithms. They cannot decide whether opaque builderSignature bytes verify under a certificate.

No clause pins RSA/ECDSA/EdDSA or another algorithm, certificate/public-key extraction, signature encoding and bounds, prehashed-versus-internal-hash semantics, or a validation operation. builderRootDigest is only a 64-hex digest of an ambiguously named member; it does not supply those missing semantics.

The preimage is also not reproducible in all admitted P values. kernelRelease is the UTS_RELEASE string from a linux_banner, but the contract defines no release grammar, unique occurrence rule, or selection rule. Multiple candidate strings yield different compact JSON preimages and signature verdicts.

A strict implementation therefore sees zero representable kernel-builder-root members or lacks an algorithm with which to verify. A permissive implementation must invent an extra role field and signature semantics. Those are different verdicts for identical signed inputs, so 'builderAttestation verifies' is not an executable structural proof.
blockers.impact: The sole structural kexec-absent proof cannot be evaluated reproducibly. Literal closed-schema implementations reject every Linux machine, while implementations that mistake a digest identity for signature verification can accept an unauthenticated capability assertion and leave post-boot replacement open.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a representable signed root-role field in the closed carrier schema and bind it to exact certificate/public-key bytes. Pin the public-key/certificate format, allowed signature algorithm and parameters, signature serialization and size, exact hash/prehash semantics, root authorization and rotation, builderRootDigest input/equality, domain-separated canonical preimage, and a unique bounded kernelRelease parse. Add valid-signature, wrong-key, wrong-member, altered-token, malformed-signature, duplicate-root, absent-role, and multiple-linux_banner vectors.

blockers.title: The same-PE official-header clause still asserts rather than verifies payload consumption
evidence: notInert now defines the in-scope stub as code at AddressOfEntryPoint and immediately states that the stub consumes the same PE official header. It still provides no canonical stub identity, instruction/relocation parser, control-flow relation, signed consume predicate, or payload measurement by which a verifier decides that statement.

The executable operations remain generic layout tests: AddressOfEntryPoint lies in some loaded executable section, and the official-header-selected range lies in one or more loaded sections. Same-file membership does not establish reachability or consumption between those ranges.

Concrete counterexample: entry section T ignores loaded section Q. Q contains the fixed-offset x86 header or unique arm64 header and names payload P; all machine, header, alignment, bounds, and loadedRange checks pass. T executes a different path. No enumerated operation distinguishes this wrapper from one whose canonical stub consumes P.

The new builderAttestation does not sign an entry-to-payload predicate or a decompressed-payload digest. It signs the whole member hashes, a capability token, and kernelRelease copied from P. Thus it can authenticate the exact wrapper and a release string while leaving the claimed T-to-P relation unproved.

This matters independently of raw-name withdrawal: optional IKCONFIG and kernelRelease are still derived from P, and honestyRepairsFromV39 claims the same-PE statement itself is the consume relation. A declarative sentence is not the requested verifying operation.
blockers.impact: The verifier cannot distinguish a canonical Linux EFI stub from a bypassing wrapper and can attribute payload-derived release/configuration facts to inert bytes. The selected payload is not proven to be the kernel path launched by the measured entry point.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a reproducible version-pinned entry-to-payload proof: for example a canonical EFI-stub identity plus exact relocation/control-transfer/header relation, direct measurement of the decompressed executed payload, or a builder predicate that explicitly signs the consume relation and payload digest. Add x86 and arm64 loaded-section decoys whose entry points ignore the official-header range.

shouldFix.title: The explicit IKCONFIG branches conflict with retained mandatory clauses
evidence: ikconfig.absentBranch says zero pairs does not refuse and both digest fields are absent. The earlier ikconfigPair still says the pair MUST be exactly one and zero pairs refuses; extract and kconfigSerialization remain unconditional. No precedence clause makes the branch override those governing steps.
fromBootLockdown.signedCarriage still unconditionally requires signedObject.ikconfigDigest to equal the derived digest, contradicting the absent branch and the corrected conditional Linux form.

kconfigSerialization.utsRelease still dereferences signedObject.buildProvenance.kernelRelease. v40's signedObject says buildProvenance is removed and MUST NOT appear inside the extras-rejected Linux form, so the present branch requires a field the closed form forbids.

The same zero-marker input is therefore accepted by absentBranch and rejected by ikconfigPair/signedCarriage; the present branch is likewise blocked by the nonexistent buildProvenance path. PTCB-V39-S2 is not repaired by adding branch prose alongside the old pipeline.
shouldFix.impact: The present and absent branches have no single executable interpretation. Independent validators can disagree, or literal validation can reject every Linux form despite a valid builder attestation.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Remove or explicitly supersede the mandatory pair/extract/serialization pipeline on the absent branch, replace the obsolete buildProvenance dereference with the exact builderAttestation release relation, make signedCarriage conditional, and propagate one branch discriminator through result, authenticatedKernelMember, signedObject, later event, refusal surfaces, and tests.

shouldFix.title: The closed successor changes linuxStanding outside its roster
evidence: A duplicate-key-free recursive semantic diff from v39 to v40 finds 51 changed leaves and exactly one outside basedOn.method's closed roster: /identityEvidenceUnion/pathlessClasses/linuxStanding.

The clause changes from measuredBootBind plus kexecAbsenceDerivation and an IKCONFIG-enabled refusal to measuredBootBind plus builderAttestation and a missing/unverified-builder refusal. That is a normative proof-authority change, not formatting.

The roster names identityEvidenceUnion.tags.PLATFORM-ATTESTED...pathlessCeremony, which is not an ancestor of pathlessClasses.linuxStanding. The claim that every unrostered path is unchanged is therefore false.
shouldFix.impact: The successor cannot be reproduced under its own closed-change discipline; reviewers following the roster can miss a normative qualification change.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add the exact linuxStanding path, or a deliberate containing ancestor, to the closed roster and reissue with a truthful semantic-diff statement.

shouldFix.title: builderRootDigest is promised on the later event but absent from its closed shape and join
evidence: signedAttestation says builderAttestation.signature is retained on the Linux later event as builderSignature plus builderRootDigest.

signedObject requires both fields, but laterEventVariant contains builderSignature only. Its closed key set has no builderRootDigest, and the tag join compares only later.builderSignature to signedObject.builderSignature.

No explicit equality binds signedObject.builderRootDigest to the selected root member's DIGEST-BOUND identityEvidence.digest. The prose 'digest of the member' also does not name exact input bytes or the digest field.
shouldFix.impact: The signed-to-observed record loses the claimed root identity, and the closed later-event schema contradicts its own retention promise. Root selection and rotation cannot be audited from the retained event as specified.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add builderRootDigest to laterEventVariant and the tag join, bind it fieldwise to the signed value and exact verified-root digest input, or remove the false retention claim and specify the single location where root identity remains auditable.
